PORTFOLIO REVIEW: Three winners working (IT +6.7%, ULTA +6.7%, NVDA +4.8%) but AMP is deeply concerning at -9.83% — this is the SECOND AMP position, the first was stopped at -3.81%. AMP is NOT appearing in today's screened candidates, which signals it has failed either the quality or (more likely) the trend filter, meaning it is in a confirmed downtrend. At -9.83% on an $9,373 position, the thesis appears broken. I strongly recommend manually exiting AMP; the rules prevent me from generating a formal SELL ticket for a name not on the screened list, but the plain-language advice is: close AMP. FOXA also does not appear in the screened list but is only -1.8% — watch closely. IT and ULTA are positive and likely simply outside the top-30 by setup score; hold both. NVDA remains in confirmed uptrend and is in the list — hold.

MARKET REGIME: SPY uptrend, +1.4% vs SMA50, slope +1.35%. Constructive backdrop, but our 0% win rate (0W/9L) demands extreme selectivity. Cash is not a failure.

NEW TRADE RATIONALE: ADBE is the single genuinely asymmetric setup. Fundamentally it is among the highest-quality franchises on the screen: ROE 61.9%, op margin 34.8%, FCF $9.3B, fwd P/E 8.59, PEG 0.58 — deeply discounted for a wide-moat software platform. The AI disruption fear has been priced in aggressively (stock down from $360 to $193 52w low). Technically it is basing at 26% of its 52-week range with the SMA50 slope just turning positive (+1.2%), which matches the preferred Stage 1→Stage 2 basing criterion. Earnings are 56 days out (Dec 9), removing near-term binary event risk. Most other top-ranked candidates (EOG, MPC, MRVL, ADI, KEYS, AME) are at 80-100% of their 52-week range and explicitly excluded by the AVOID rule. TEL, GNRC, GEHC, HUBB all report earnings within 14 days — too risky to initiate. One focused position in ADBE, sized to risk 1.5% of equity, is the correct answer here. Return rest to cash.
